questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A lively city with a different culture than the one I am used to.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The experience was good. The bureaucracy in order to do the exchange is a mess. And the communication between home and host university is non-exciting.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Massimo Costa at the Erasmus office in Milan was very helpful and responsive through email, which made things easier. Information about residence etc. was very limited (actually I only received a document to show upon my arrival with no information)

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not receive any assistance as such. The only contact I had to anything related to Erasmus, was when I picked up my student card at the office.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The help and information is very limited.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was great living in a student residence. Made the exchange experience very good. It was easy to get accommodation as this was offered when I applied for the exchange.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is a good experience and if there are any questions, always ask the people who live there. They know more about the place than any of the employees at the university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to sign up through the university's system, which is a bit outdated in my opinion. With that being said, everything worked out fine.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I did not seek any help.  æ

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I registered to all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: As registration is the same for both the regular students and erasmus students, you can always ask someone who is more familiar with the system.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses seemed easier in Milan than in Copenhagen. And also the expectations of different professors varies a lot in my experience.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching was different, as it was often smaller classes with fewer people than what is the case in UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: International Political Thought, Global Challenges to Democracy, Datafied Society, Democracy and Development and Social and Political Attitudes.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Social and Political Attitudes, as professor Vezzoni is really nice and also challenged me to reflect in different ways about methodology in social sciences.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I did not encounter any unexpected costs as such.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The living expenses were generally higher than expected. Food and groceries are quite expensive, as Milan is probably the most expensive city in Italy.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not attend any.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I did not attend any.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Enjoy life with other exchange students and talk to the people at the dorm if you accepted student housing. Go on trips around the country. Italy is beautiful.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Como, Garda and the other lakes. Spend time in the city with friends and enjoy the food and the beautiful surroundings.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It took a bit of adjustment. Patience is key if you are from Scandinavia and also a lot of people do not speak English very well.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Stay at a dorm and talk to the people who live there.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: People were not unambitious but more calm in their approach to life. Not planning to much and living in the presence.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciated how eating together, drinking coffee etc. is a social event that people enjoy every day.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Stay at a dorm, but a metro card and ask the people around you when you are in doubt.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do not do 30 ECTS in one trimester. Split them in two trimesters to have more time to enjoy Italy.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making friends, experiencing different culture and living in a beautiful city.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Doing too many exams in too short a period of time. And sometimes also getting out and socializing enough. My home university did not help me to get in touch with other danish exchange students either, so I had to do this myself, which is quite a shame.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
